components.name: invite-people
components.title: Invite People
components.description: Invite a teammate by email, validate the address and update the member list.
useCases: In project settings, an admin enters a designer’s email. The app sends the invitation through onInvite and the form keeps the address if delivery fails.
When setting up a team, the organizer checks the existing members before inviting the next colleague.

components.name: focus-mode
components.title: Focus Mode
components.description: Silence notifications for the duration of a focus session.
useCases: Before reviewing a mockup, a designer starts a 25-minute session. The notification stack collapses and the timer shows the time left.
In a learning workspace, a student turns on focus for an exercise. The app uses onChange to pause its own notification popups.

notifications.type: { title: string; body: string; time: string; }[] | undefined

components.name: swipe-deck
components.title: Swipe Deck
components.description: Swipe through a stack of art prints to reveal the next poster.
components.usage: <SwipeDeck cards={[{ title: "Orbit", color: "#bed5ce", ink: "#20312a" }, { title: "Fold", color: "#dbcfbd", ink: "#30271c" }]} />
useCases: On a portfolio page, a visitor swipes through a poster series one piece at a time.
When shortlisting covers, an editor swipes a candidate right to keep it. The app records the card and direction from onSwipe.

components.name: glass-player
components.title: Glass Player
components.description: An audio player with cover art, seeking, repeat and mute.
useCases: On a lesson page, a student scrubs back to a phrase they missed in an audio explanation.
In a music catalog, a buyer loops a track preview to compare its arrangement with another version.

components.name: stat-card
components.title: Stat Card
components.description: Explore individual data points and switch reporting periods.
useCases: On an editorial dashboard, a team member switches page views from daily to weekly to see how readership changed.
In a support report, a manager selects a chart point to read the ticket count for a specific period.

components.name: magnetic-button
components.title: Magnetic Button
components.description: The button follows your pointer and springs back into place.
useCases: On a studio homepage, a visitor presses “View portfolio.” The app opens the collection through onClick.
At the end of a presentation, a “Try the demo” button responds to the approaching pointer and opens the demo when pressed.

components.name: plan-switch
components.title: Plan Switch
components.description: Switch billing periods to compare the monthly price, total and savings.
components.usage: <PlanSwitch options={["Monthly", "Yearly"]} prices={[{ monthly: 20, total: 20 }, { monthly: 15, total: 180 }]} />
useCases: On a pricing page, a buyer compares the monthly price with the annual total before subscribing.
At renewal, a customer changes the billing period. The app uses the selected index to send the corresponding plan to checkout.

components.name: wave-slider
components.title: Wave Slider
components.description: A compact volume control that remembers the level before muting.
useCases: In a player, a listener sets volume on a 0–100 scale. The app converts the percentage to an audio level.
In an ambient sound editor, the app restores the saved level through value and updates the mix as the user moves the slider.

components.name: flip-counter
components.title: Flip Counter
components.description: Digits roll into place as the count changes.
useCases: When booking a table, a guest adds people up to the table’s seating capacity.
In a print order, a customer changes the number of copies. The app recalculates the quote from the new count.

components.name: hold-button
components.title: Hold to Confirm
components.description: Hold to fill the button and confirm the action.
useCases: Before clearing a draft, the author holds the button to confirm. Releasing it early preserves the text.
At a kiosk, an operator holds the session reset button. The app starts the reset after onConfirm.

components.name: spring-dock
components.title: Spring Dock
components.description: The indicator slides under the selected item.
useCases: In a layout editor, a designer picks a tool by its icon. The app maps the button index to a canvas tool.
In a creator workspace, a bottom dock opens the library, drafts and publications, highlighting the active section.

components.name: file-drop
components.title: File Drop
components.description: Drop files into a folder and see their names and sizes.
useCases: When opening a support ticket, a customer drops screenshots. The form receives File objects and attaches them when the ticket is submitted.
In a gallery editor, an author selects images from disk. The app previews the chosen files before upload.

components.name: rolling-text
components.title: Rolling Text
components.description: Letters roll into place one by one.
useCases: At an exhibition kiosk, a visitor taps the greeting to read it in the next language.
In a brand type specimen, a designer cycles through short words with the arrow keys to compare letterforms.

components.name: spring-switch
components.title: Spring Switch
components.description: A spring-loaded switch for on/off settings.
useCases: In profile settings, a user enables notifications. The app saves the flag and restores it on the next visit.
In a layout editor, a user temporarily enables a grid. The local switch tells the canvas when to show its guides.

components.name: bloom-menu
components.title: Bloom Menu
components.description: Actions fan out around the menu button.
useCases: Beside a selected shape, a designer expands duplicate and delete actions and applies one to that shape.
On a photo card, an editor opens a compact menu to download the original or copy its link through an app handler.

components.name: morph-tooltip
components.title: Morph Tooltip
components.description: Hover or focus with the keyboard
useCases: In a reading list, a reader opens an article’s actions and bookmarks it for later.
On a research board, a contributor pins an important reference. The app handles the pin action for that entry.

components.name: command-button
components.title: Command Button
components.description: Run the command
useCases: In an invoice preview, an operator starts printing with one button. The app opens the print dialog in onExecute.
In a command demo, a developer repeats an operation and sees how many times it was invoked.

components.name: loading-success
components.title: Loading Success
components.description: Start the action and wait for the result
components.usage: <LoadingSuccess onRun={async () => { const response = await fetch("/api/status"); if (!response.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + response.status); }} />
useCases: In integration settings, an admin tests a connection. The button waits for the server and offers another attempt if the check fails.
In a report, an analyst starts a sync and sees confirmation once the request completes.

components.name: copy-button
components.title: Copy Button
components.description: Copy the text
useCases: In documentation, a developer copies the entire installation command and pastes it into a terminal.
On an order page, a customer copies the ticket number for a support email and gets confirmation.

components.name: like-burst
components.title: Like Burst
components.description: Add or remove a like
useCases: In a community feed, a reader likes a post and immediately sees its count change.
On an illustration page, a viewer presses again to remove their like. The app saves the new flag through onChange.

components.name: slide-to-confirm
components.title: Slide To Confirm
components.description: Slide into the finish zone to confirm. An incomplete swipe returns the handle.
useCases: At a packing station, a worker slides to confirm after inspecting a parcel. The app marks it ready to ship.
On a mobile terminal, an operator ends a shift with a deliberate slide so a stray tap cannot close the shift.

components.name: cart-button
components.title: Cart Button
components.description: Expand the cart to adjust quantities and see the total.
useCases: In a print catalog, a shopper adds the first copy and adjusts the quantity directly on the product card.
At a merchandise kiosk, a shopper removes an extra item. The app receives the new quantity and updates the order total.

components.name: undo-button
components.title: Undo Button
components.description: Delete the entry and undo the change
useCases: In a draft list, an author removes an entry and restores it immediately after spotting a mistaken selection.
In a reading collection, an editor temporarily excludes an article. The app updates its visibility and supports undo.

components.name: bell-button
components.title: Bell Button
components.description: Toggle notifications
useCases: On a project page, a member subscribes to updates and presses again to unsubscribe.
On a livestream page, a viewer enables a reminder. The app uses the new flag to schedule a notification.

components.name: unlock-face-id
components.title: Unlock Face ID
components.description: Try the scan demo
useCases: In an interactive prototype, a client tries a simulated scan and sees the unlocked file state.
In a protected vault UI, a user starts verification. The app runs its authentication mechanism and passes the result through status.

components.name: spring-dropdown
components.title: Spring Dropdown
components.description: Open the list and choose a status
useCases: In an illustration editor, an author selects a file format from a short list before exporting.
In an order list, a manager selects a sort order. The app receives the chosen option and reorders the list.

components.name: morph-island
components.title: Morph Island
components.description: A compact panel for a timer, an export and an incoming call.
useCases: In an incoming-call prototype, a user accepts or declines a call. The app receives the decision through onCall.
In a mobile UI presentation, a designer cycles through the built-in activities to show a timer and operation progress in one compact panel.

components.name: tab-pill
components.title: Tab Pill
components.description: Switch tabs
useCases: In a setup guide, a developer switches between API and CLI tabs to read the relevant snippet.
In a material description, a shopper opens care instructions beside the specifications without leaving the product page.

components.name: segmented-control
components.title: Segmented Control
components.description: Choose a period
useCases: In a performance report, an analyst switches between p50 and p95. The app supplies the series for the selected metric.
In a file manager, a user chooses a grid or list. The app changes how it displays the same files.

components.name: rubber-dock
components.title: Rubber Dock
components.description: Move across the icons
useCases: In a workspace shell, a user moves from Files to Calendar using the built-in four-section dock.
In a mobile desktop prototype, a designer moves across the dock, previews its labels and selects Photos.

components.name: dynamic-menu
components.title: Dynamic Menu
components.description: Open the menu and explore a submenu
useCases: In a diagram editor, an author opens the export submenu and selects SVG. The app starts the corresponding exporter.
In a report builder, an analyst opens the format list, goes back a level and revisits the export choice.

components.name: sidebar-collapse
components.title: Sidebar Collapse
components.description: A studio sidebar that switches between workspaces.
useCases: In a design workspace, a designer collapses navigation to make room for the canvas while retaining access to both sections.
In a studio workspace, a teammate selects Projects or Collections. The app switches content using the section index.

components.name: pagination-dots
components.title: Pagination Dots
components.description: Go to another page
useCases: In a product gallery, a shopper jumps to a particular photo using the dots below the image.
In an onboarding tour, a user jumps to the last screen with the keyboard. The app displays the slide at the selected index.

components.name: command-palette
components.title: Command Palette
components.description: Find and run a command
useCases: In an editor, a user types part of a command name and runs the matching action with Enter.
In an admin console, an operator finds the command for opening the ticket queue. The app maps the selected command to its route.

components.name: step-progress
components.title: Step Progress
components.description: Move to the next step
useCases: In an application form, a customer moves through contact details, options and review. The app shows the fields for the selected step.
In a setup wizard, an admin returns to a numbered step to correct settings before finishing.

components.name: toolbar
components.title: Toolbar
components.description: Toggle text formatting
useCases: In a note editor, an author turns on bold and italic and immediately sees the combination in a text sample.
In a template builder, a designer removes one style. The app receives the remaining styles for the selected label.

components.name: morph-popover
components.title: Morph Popover
components.description: Open the feedback button to leave a comment
useCases: A reader spots an error in the docs and sends feedback from a small form beside the article.
During a mockup review, a designer leaves a short comment. If the service is unavailable, they retry from the same form.

components.name: letter-limit
components.title: Letter Limit
components.description: Type until you reach the character limit
useCases: On a profile page, an author trims their bio to the platform limit and sees how much space it uses.
When writing a short caption, an editor pastes text containing emoji. The field enforces the limit without splitting combined characters.

components.name: springy-input
components.title: Springy Input
components.description: Focus the field and start typing
useCases: In a knowledge base, a teammate enters a question and submits it with Enter. The app opens the results page.
In a swatch catalog, a designer types part of a name. The app uses onChange to filter swatches as they type.

components.name: otp-code
components.title: OTP Code
components.description: Enter or paste a numeric code
useCases: At sign-in, a user pastes a one-time code from a message. The app submits the complete code for verification, including leading zeros.
When confirming a new email, a user enters four digits. The app sets the field length to match its verification code.

components.name: star-rating
components.title: Star Rating
components.description: Rate from one to five stars
useCases: After a class, a student rates the lesson. The app records the selected number of stars against that lesson.
In a prototype gallery, a participant rates each design. The app collects the scores for comparison.

components.name: tag-input
components.title: Tag Input
components.description: Type a tag and press Enter
useCases: Before publishing an article, an editor adds topics, removes an accidental tag and saves the resulting list.
In a media library, a teammate opens an asset’s existing keywords and adds more so it is easier to find later.

components.name: password-strength
components.title: Password Strength
components.description: Watch the strength indicator as you type
useCases: At signup, a user watches the local strength estimate change as they type a new password.
In a password change form, a user improves the candidate before submitting. The app applies its own policy when saving.

components.name: checkbox-list
components.title: Checkbox List
components.description: Check off completed items
useCases: When exporting a report, an analyst selects the sections to include. The app builds the file from those choices.
In newsletter settings, a subscriber selects topics of interest and saves several preferences at once.

components.name: jelly-slider
components.title: Jelly Slider
components.description: Drag the elastic handle
useCases: In a sticker editor, a designer moves an opacity slider. The app applies the selected percentage to the sticker.
In a motion demo, a visitor adjusts an effect’s intensity and sees the numeric value beside the slider.

components.name: detent-dial
components.title: Detent Dial
components.description: Turn the dial with the arrow keys or a swipe
useCases: On a synthesizer panel, a musician turns a dial to select one of eleven effect levels.
In a lamp prototype, a designer selects a brightness step. The app maps the 0–10 position to a light output level.

components.name: exposure-slider
components.title: Exposure Slider
components.description: Adjust photo brightness in EV and restore the original exposure.
useCases: A photographer adjusts portrait exposure and compares the preview with the original before saving.
In a photography lesson, a learner tries negative and positive exposure adjustments on one frame, then resets to zero.

components.name: wheel-picker
components.title: Wheel Picker
components.description: Scroll to a value
useCases: When setting up a profile, a user scrolls through time zones and saves their selection.
In a mobile timer, a user selects a duration from preset intervals. The app maps the selection to a timer value.

components.name: scrubber
components.title: Scrubber
components.description: Scrub the timeline
useCases: In an animation preview, a designer scrubs to an individual frame to inspect an object’s position.
When reviewing an experiment recording, a researcher selects a sample number. The app displays the data for that position.

components.name: receipt-printer
components.title: Receipt Printer
components.description: Confirm a payment, watch the thermal receipt print and print another copy.
components.usage: <ReceiptPrinter merchant="Studio" order={{ id: "S-12", description: "Print", amount: 32, currency: "EUR" }} />
useCases: After checkout, a shop shows a receipt with the order ID returned by its server. The buyer can print that confirmed receipt again.
In a point-of-sale prototype, a designer runs a demo purchase and shows the receipt without connecting a payment service.

components.name: card-field
components.title: Card Field
components.description: Try the test card
useCases: In a checkout prototype, a tester selects the built-in test card and resets it for the next run.
In a live checkout, a customer fills in Stripe Elements over HTTPS. The app uses onCompleteChange to decide when to offer payment confirmation.

components.name: signature-pad
components.title: Signature Pad
components.description: Draw a signature and save it
components.usage: <SignaturePad onSave={png => { const link = document.createElement("a"); link.download = "signature.png"; link.href = png; link.click(); }} />
useCases: At equipment pickup, the recipient signs with a finger. The app attaches the resulting PNG to the pickup record.
In a greeting card editor, an author adds a handwritten autograph, undoes a stray stroke and saves the drawing.

components.name: parallax-ticket
components.title: Parallax Ticket
components.description: Move the pointer to tilt the ticket
useCases: On a concert page, a visitor explores the ticket artwork and flips it over to see the date.
In an identity design portfolio, a designer presents a pass mockup with custom artwork, an event name and a date.

components.name: glass-lens
components.title: Glass Lens
components.description: Move the lens over the artwork
useCases: On a fabric product page, a shopper moves the lens over a photo to inspect the weave.
During a design review, a designer magnifies a screenshot detail and moves the lens with the arrow keys.

components.name: pull-refresh
components.title: Pull Refresh
components.description: Pull down to sync a file. A short pull cancels the gesture.
components.usage: <PullRefresh onRefresh={async () => { const result = await fetch("/api/status", { cache: "no-store" }); if (!result.ok) throw new Error("Refresh failed"); }} />
useCases: In a mobile recent-files panel, a teammate pulls down to refresh. The app requests fresh data in onRefresh.
After a connection drops, a user retries the sync with the button and reads its status to see whether the request completed.

components.name: expand-card
components.title: Expand Card
components.description: Select a collection to reveal its cover and details
useCases: In a collection list, a shopper opens a card, reads the details and returns to the overview.
In a workshop listing, an organizer puts the full session description behind a compact cover that visitors can expand.

components.name: fan-cards
components.title: Fan Cards
components.description: Fan out the deck and lift the card under your pointer.
useCases: In an illustrator’s portfolio, a visitor fans out labeled cards to see which works belong to a series.
In a card-game demo, a player fans out their hand and moves the pointer across it to lift an individual card.

components.name: profile-card
components.title: Profile Card
components.description: Follow the profile to see the count and actions change
useCases: In a mentor directory, a student opens a conversation with a particular mentor. The app receives the name through onMessage.
In a community, a reader follows an author from their profile card. The app persists the follow state.

components.name: boarding-pass
components.title: Boarding Pass
components.description: A boarding pass with route, gate and an expandable barcode.
useCases: On a trip screen, a passenger expands the boarding pass to check their seat, gate and boarding time.
In a connecting itinerary, the app shows a separate pass for each flight so the traveler can distinguish the legs of the trip.

components.name: notification-stack
components.title: Notification Stack
components.description: Expand the stack or swipe a notification away
useCases: On a team dashboard, a teammate reviews stacked build notifications and dismisses the ones they have read.
In an activity center, the app updates notifications with stable IDs while the user works through the remaining cards.

components.name: page-flip
components.title: Page Flip
components.description: Turn a double-sided page around its spine.
useCases: In a digital booklet, a visitor flips through short chapter captions like pages in a printed edition.
In a visual concept presentation, a designer shows one idea per spread and moves in either direction with the arrow keys.

components.name: stack-panel
components.title: Stack Panel
components.description: Open a project and swipe right to go back
useCases: In compact settings, a user moves from the root menu into notification preferences and then goes back one level.
In product help, a reader picks a topic. The app displays the associated content in the same panel through renderPanel.

components.name: weight-wave
components.title: Weight Wave
components.description: Move across the letters or tap
useCases: On a type studio’s page, a visitor moves across a word to see how the weight of nearby letters changes.
In an interactive wordmark specimen, a designer moves the emphasis across letters with the keyboard to inspect each shape.

components.name: goo-morph
components.title: Goo Morph
components.description: Switch the liquid lettering
useCases: In a brand presentation, a viewer taps a keyword to reveal the next principle in the series.
In a motion showcase, a designer supplies their own words to compare transitions between short and long names.

components.name: scramble-text
components.title: Scramble Text
components.description: Reveal the scrambled text
useCases: On a game promo page, a visitor triggers a decoding effect that reveals the mission name.
In a release presentation, the presenter reveals the version’s codename as an animated label.

components.name: read-along
components.title: Read Along
components.description: Words light up at reading speed. Pause or step through them individually.
useCases: In a language lesson, a learner starts word-by-word highlighting and pauses at a difficult phrase.
When rehearsing a short speech, a speaker selects a word midway through the text and resumes at the chosen pace.

components.name: roll-links
components.title: Roll Links
components.description: Hover or focus the link
useCases: In portfolio navigation, a visitor sees a hover response on a section name and follows its link.
At the end of an article, a reader focuses the documentation link with the keyboard and opens it without a mouse.

components.name: marker-text
components.title: Marker Text
components.description: Highlight the phrase
useCases: In lecture notes, an instructor taps a short quotation to highlight it during an explanation.
During a presentation, an editor highlights a key point and clears the mark before showing it again.

components.name: dynamic-text
components.title: Dynamic Text
components.description: Change the word in the headline
useCases: In a product-family heading, the brand name stays fixed while a visitor taps through the product names.
In a classroom example, a student changes the ending of a short phrase to explore combinations with a fixed opening.

components.name: typewriter
components.title: Typewriter
components.description: Start typing the text
useCases: In a terminal demo, a reader starts the character-by-character reveal of a prepared command.
On a game introduction screen, the author chooses a slow reveal so the player can read a line as dialogue.

components.name: music-toggle
components.title: Music Toggle
components.description: Toggle the equalizer animation
useCases: On an exhibition site, a visitor enables background music. The app starts the track when the toggle changes.
In an interactive story, a reader turns off the soundtrack and continues reading in silence.

components.name: prompt-box
components.title: Prompt Box
components.description: Enter a prompt and send it
components.usage: <PromptBox suggestions={["Explain this example"]} onSend={text => localStorage.setItem("last-prompt", text)} />
useCases: On an assistant’s empty screen, an analyst picks “Summarize the report,” refines the prompt and submits it.
In a writing assistant, an author enters a custom request. The app returns its request promise so the form shows progress and allows a retry on failure.

components.name: streaming-reply
components.title: Streaming Reply
components.description: Reveal the reply in chunks
useCases: In a chatbot demo, a visitor starts the gradual reveal of a prepared reply and watches the words appear.
In a worked example, a learner reads an explanation in stages. The app supplies the completed text for playback.

components.name: ghost-suggestion
components.title: Ghost Suggestion
components.description: Start typing and accept the suggestion with the right arrow
useCases: In a travel form, a user starts typing a city and completes its name from a matching suggestion.
In a command field, a developer enters the prefix of a known command. The app supplies the vocabulary used for inline completion.

components.name: goo-thinking
components.title: Goo Thinking
components.description: Tap the dots to reveal the answer
useCases: In an assistant prototype, a designer taps the processing indicator to reveal a short sample reply.
In a search presentation, a presenter replays the transition from “Finding matches” to a prepared result.

components.name: siri-orb
components.title: Assistant Orb
components.description: Switch assistant states
useCases: In a voice assistant, the user sees when the app is listening, processing or speaking. The app passes the current state to AssistantOrb.
On a recording screen, the app supplies normalized microphone amplitude so the orb reacts to voice volume.

components.name: agent-steps
components.title: Agent Steps
components.description: Walk through the agent’s steps
useCases: In a training demo, a user advances an agent from reading a file to preparing a result and sees how many steps are complete.
During a presentation, the presenter advances each step with a button. The app uses onStep to display that step’s artifact alongside it.

components.name: tool-approval
components.title: Tool Approval
components.description: Approve or decline the action
components.usage: <ToolApproval action="Run build" resource="package.json" onDecision={allowed => console.info({ allowed })} />
useCases: Before creating an event, an assistant shows the calendar and proposed action. The user approves or declines, and the app handles the decision.
In a workspace, an agent proposes changing a specific file. The editor checks the resource name before approving the write.

components.name: thinking-text
components.title: Thinking Text
components.description: Start the thinking indicator
useCases: While an assistant gathers document context, the reader sees a short status beside the reply area.
On a report page, the app displays “Processing rows” while a background calculation runs, then replaces it with the result.

components.name: task-list
components.title: Task List
components.description: Work through the task queue
useCases: Before a release, a teammate checks off completed reviews and sees how many items remain.
In a lab workbook, a student checks off finished tasks. The app saves the completed task names through onChange.

components.name: voice-input
components.title: Voice Input
components.description: Record and play a voice note
useCases: In a discussion, a user records a voice comment and stops recording. The app attaches the resulting audio file to the message.
In a notes form, an author dictates an idea. The app sends the Blob from onRecord to its transcription service.

components.name: hold-to-publish
components.title: Hold to Publish
components.description: Hold to fill the publish button. A checkmark appears when it completes.
useCases: Before releasing an article, an editor holds the publish button. The app submits the piece to the CMS after the hold completes.
In a teaching workspace, an author starts publishing a lesson, spots a mistake and releases the button before confirming.

components.name: command-search
components.title: Command Search
components.description: Click or press ⌘/Ctrl + K to expand the search field.
useCases: In a documentation hub, a developer presses Ctrl/⌘+K, enters a phrase and opens the results page through the app handler.
In a compact project toolbar, a user expands a button into a field and searches for a file using free text.

components.name: swipe-tabs
components.title: Swipe Tabs
components.description: Swipe horizontally to move between panels and update the active tab.
useCases: On a mobile product page, a shopper swipes between the description, specifications and reviews.
In a course workspace, a student opens a link to the practice tab. The app sets the active ID and updates the URL on subsequent changes.

components.name: lesson-outline
components.title: Lesson Outline
components.description: Browse lessons and resume a course.
components.usage: <LessonOutline title="React" currentId="state" items={[{ id: "state", title: "State", href: "/lessons/state" }]} />
useCases: Returning to a course, a student sees the current lesson in the outline and resumes it with the continue button.
Before a class, a participant reviews the topic sequence and follows the link to a particular lesson.

components.name: code-exercise
components.title: Code Exercise
components.description: Edit an exercise, run a sample and investigate a failing test.
components.usage: <CodeExercise draftKey="lesson:ids:v1" initialSource="^UI-[0-9]+$" tests={[{ input: "UI-23", expected: true }]} />
useCases: In a regex lesson, a student edits a pattern, checks it against sample strings and inspects mismatches.
In a lab, a student returns to an unfinished exercise. The app assigns each exercise its own draftKey so the right draft is restored.

components.name: run-console
components.title: Run Console
components.description: Follow compilation and execution, inspect output and stop a run.
useCases: During an exercise run, a student sees the execution phase, output and duration reported by the runner.
When a run stalls or fails, a student requests a stop or jumps to the offending line through the editor’s handler.

components.name: test-results
components.title: Test Results
components.description: Inspect the input, expected value and actual result of each test.
components.usage: <TestResults results={[{ input: "UI-23", expected: true, actual: false }]} />
useCases: After checking a solution, a student selects a failing case and compares its input, expected value and actual result.
During review, a student asks about a particular mismatch. The app sends the selected case to a tutor through onAsk.

components.name: ask-tutor
components.title: Ask Tutor
components.description: Ask about a lesson or failing test with selected context.
useCases: During an exercise, a student asks about a selected code fragment. The app sends the question and its context to the tutoring service.
While investigating a mistake, a learner removes an irrelevant source before submitting and reads a reply citing the relevant lesson passage.

components.name: lesson-citation
components.title: Lesson Citation
components.description: Read a cited lesson passage and return to the exercise.
useCases: Below a tutor’s reply, a student expands a citation and checks the explanation against the original lesson passage.
In an exercise review, a reader opens the referenced textbook section. The app can take them back to the marked location through onReturn.

components.name: predict-output
components.title: Predict Output
components.description: Predict the output, compare your answer and read the explanation.
useCases: Before running an example, a student predicts its output and reads the explanation.
At a lesson checkpoint, an instructor supplies possible results for an expression. The app records the learner’s choice through onAnswer.

components.name: execution-trace
components.title: Execution Trace
components.description: Step through a trace with the active line and live variable values.
components.usage: <ExecutionTrace code={["let x = 2", "x *= 3"]} steps={[{ line: 1, variables: { x: 2 } }, { line: 2, variables: { x: 6 } }]} />
useCases: When studying a loop, a student steps through the trace and follows the counter beside the highlighted line.
When explaining a bug, an instructor goes back to the step where a variable first acquired the wrong value.

components.name: hint-ladder
components.title: Hint Ladder
components.description: Reveal hints one at a time, from a question to a related example.
useCases: When stuck on a problem, a student opens a general hint first and requests the next one only if needed.
In a lab, an instructor arranges hints from a general idea to a concrete step. The app records how far each learner went.

components.name: channel-list
components.title: Channel List
components.description: Course channels and direct conversations.
components.usage: <ChannelList workspace="Studio" channels={[{ id: "design", name: "design", kind: "channel", topic: "Review" }]} />
useCases: In a course sidebar, a student selects their cohort’s channel. The app opens the conversation by its stable ID.
In team chat, a colleague switches from a shared channel to a direct conversation. The list highlights the selection controlled by the app.

components.name: chat-composer
components.title: Chat Composer
components.description: Compose a draft, insert line breaks and track delivery.
useCases: On a ticket page, a customer submits a comment. If the network is unavailable, the typed text stays in the field for another attempt.
When switching conversations, an operator can return to an unfinished reply. The app stores one draft per conversation and supplies it through value.

components.name: message-reactions
components.title: Message Reactions
components.description: Message reactions with participant counts.
useCases: Under a release announcement, a teammate adds a reaction and sees the count update beside the emoji.
In a proposal thread, a member removes their reaction. The app updates that emoji’s count while preserving everyone else’s reactions.

components.name: chat-post
components.title: Chat Post
components.description: Render one chat message with an author, text, optional code and a resource link.
components.usage: <ChatPostBody post={{ id: "release", author: "Sam", initials: "S", time: "10:00", text: "v2.0" }} />
useCases: In a support log, a reader sees a single message with its author, time and code snippet, even on a page without a reply editor.
In a course feed, an instructor shares a workbook link. The card shows the resource below the text, and the app adds reactions through children.

components.name: message-thread
components.title: Message Thread
components.description: Threaded replies with the original message and a separate composer.
components.usage: <MessageThread parent={{ id: "24", author: "Sam", initials: "S", time: "10:00", text: "PR #24" }} />
useCases: In a design review, a designer opens a comment thread and replies with the original message visible above the discussion.
In support, an operator switches between threads. The app keeps each thread’s draft separate from its posted replies.

components.name: course-messenger
components.title: Course Messenger
components.description: A workspace for course channels, direct messages and threads.
components.usage: <CourseMessenger workspace="Studio" channels={[{ id: "design", name: "design", kind: "channel", topic: "Review" }]} initialMessages={{ design: [] }} />
useCases: In a course workspace, a student discusses an assignment in the cohort channel and opens a thread for a specific question.
In a team workspace, a colleague moves between direct and shared conversations. The app synchronizes messages and reactions with its server.

onSend.type: ((channelId: string, text: string, parentId?: string) => void | Promise<void>) | undefined

onToggleReaction.type: ((channelId: string, postId: string, emoji: string) => void) | undefined

components.name: latency-chart
components.title: Latency Chart
components.description: Response times by percentile and sample.
components.usage: <LatencyChart title="API latency" unit="ms" samples={[{ label: "10:00", p50: 18, p95: 42 }, { label: "10:05", p50: 20, p95: null }]} />
useCases: After a release, an engineer compares median API latency with p95 to spot slowdowns affecting a subset of requests.
During incident review, an on-call engineer steps through samples and distinguishes a missing measurement from a measured zero.

components.name: conversion-funnel
components.title: Conversion Funnel
components.description: Participant counts and conversion between consecutive stages.
components.usage: <ConversionFunnel stages={[{ id: "visit", label: "Visit", count: 120 }, { id: "signup", label: "Signup", count: 36 }]} />
useCases: In a store report, an analyst compares counts at the cart, checkout and purchase stages to find the biggest drop-off.
A course team compares signups, first lessons and completions. The app supplies the participant count for each stage.

components.name: cohort-retention
components.title: Cohort Retention
components.description: Cohort retention with missing observations distinguished from zero.
components.usage: <CohortRetention cohorts={[{ id: "w1", label: "W01", size: 80, retained: [80, 45, null] }]} />
useCases: In a subscription report, an analyst compares the share of users in different signup cohorts who returned a week later.
In a course dashboard, a curriculum lead distinguishes a future cohort week from a completed week in which nobody returned.

components.name: issue-board
components.title: Issue Board
components.description: A kanban board with status transitions and inline issue creation.
components.usage: <IssueBoard defaultIssues={[{ id: "UI-7", title: "Search", status: "active", priority: "high", points: 3 }]} />
useCases: At stand-up, a developer moves a card from backlog to active so the team sees the task’s new status.
During intake, a manager creates a task directly on the board. The app saves the updated list and refreshes its other views.

components.name: issue-table
components.title: Issue Table
components.description: An inline-editable issue database with sortable priorities.
components.usage: <IssueTable defaultIssues={[{ id: "UI-7", title: "Search", status: "active", priority: "high", points: 3 }]} />
useCases: During backlog triage, a manager sorts issues by priority and corrects a title inline.
In a team meeting, a coordinator changes a task’s status in the table. The board receives the same updated array and shows the new status.

components.name: cycle-planner
components.title: Cycle Planner
components.description: Plan cycle scope against capacity using issue estimates.
components.usage: <CyclePlanner cycleId="Q2" capacity={12} defaultIssues={[{ id: "UI-7", title: "Search", status: "active", priority: "high", points: 3, cycleId: "Q2" }]} />
useCases: Before a sprint, a team adds estimated issues to a cycle and sees how many points still fit.
When capacity changes, a lead removes an issue from the cycle and checks whether the plan is back within budget.
